transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. To get us started, could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Um... I guess my husband wanted me to come in. Him and the people at the warehouse, they keep acting like I'm crazy. But I'm not. I just... I know they've been watching my moves at work. They keep changing the pallet counts on me just to keep me from getting that supervisor spot. I don't really know what else to say about it.
Do you ever hear any voices or sounds that other people around you don't seem to hear?

Um... I guess. Maybe sometimes. I don't really like talking about it, but... yeah. Like if I'm in the aisle at work, or just at home folding clothes, I'll hear this man's voice. It sounds clear as day. He just tells me, Nicole, check it again. But there's nobody anywhere near me when it happens. I don't really know what else to say about it.
How long have you been experiencing these thoughts about your coworkers and hearing this voice?
Um... I don't know. A while, I guess. Maybe... about eight months? Yeah, around eight months since it all started. The voice, and... them messing with my stuff. That's about it.

Do you find that, when you are talking to your husband or coworkers, they sometimes have trouble understanding what you are trying to say because your thoughts feel jumbled or your sentences don't seem to make sense?

Um... yeah, I guess so. Sometimes. My husband says that. When I try to tell him about the warehouse, about the forklift sheets... I don't know, it just goes from that to the signs outside the church, and then how he's talking to me. I guess my words just run together. People say they can't follow me. I just... I don't know. That's what they say.
Since these things started eight months ago, have you found it more difficult to keep up with your normal daily tasks, like keeping up with chores or taking care of your personal hygiene?
Um... no. Not really. I still go to work and... do my laundry and stuff. I shower. It's just normal, I guess. I haven't really noticed a problem with any of that.
Do you feel like you have lost interest in the things you used to enjoy, or do you find it difficult to get motivated to do things you usually like to do?

Um... I don't know. I guess I don't do much anymore. When I'm at home, I mostly just... sit quiet. I just stare at the TV, or look at my phone. My husband, he tries to joke with me sometimes to get a reaction, but... I don't know. I just don't feel much come across my face. I just sit there.
Have you ever had any periods of time, lasting at least a couple of weeks, where you felt extremely down, hopeless, or had almost no energy?
Um... no. Not really. I don't think so. I mean, I have normal days, I guess. I don't remember feeling like that.

When you are talking to your husband or interacting with others, have they ever mentioned that you might be laughing at things that aren't funny, or that your facial expressions don't seem to match what you are talking about?
Um... no. Not really. I don't think he's ever said anything like that to me. I just... I don't know, I just talk to him normally, I guess.
Have you ever felt like your body gets stuck in a certain position, or have you ever found yourself unable to move or speak for a period of time?

Um... no, not stuck like that. I don't get frozen or anything. But... at work, I guess I do things... a certain way sometimes. Like, I'll walk the exact same path around the pallets... over and over. And I have to line the labels up just right before I move them. My lead told me to stop doing it, but... I just kind of have to.
When you are speaking to others, do they ever tell you that your speech is so disorganized or incoherent that they cannot follow what you are trying to say?

Um... yeah, sometimes. I guess. People say that... they can't follow me. Like... I try to explain something, and... I don't know, my words just go from the forklift sheets at work to... the signs at church... and then maybe how my husband's sounding. It makes sense to me, but... they say they don't get it.
When you think about the people at the warehouse watching you and changing the pallet counts, do you have a specific, detailed theory about why they are doing this or how they are accomplishing it?

Um... well, it's pretty obvious. They're... they're doing it to stop me. I mean, my husband and the people at work... they all act like I'm the one who's crazy. But I know they're watching everything I do. They mess with the pallet counts because... well, because they don't want me to get that supervisor spot. That's why I'm even here... because of how they're acting about it.
